newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: New Czech finance minister cast in PM's mould.
newsitem.headline: New Czech finance minister cast in PM's mould.

text.p: Ivan Pilip, chosen as finance minister on Wednesday by the Czech Republic's centre-right coalition, is a young economist who hitched his career early to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
Pilip, aged 33, rose in 1993 to become the chairman of the small conservative Christian Democratic Union, a partner in the Klaus-led coalition which came to power after 1992 general elections.
When his party merged with Klaus's Civic Democratic Party ahead of 1996 elections Pilip became a party vice-chairman under Klaus then education minister in a new cabinet formed last June.

He takes over the Finance Ministry from Ivan Kocarnik, who quit last weekend and was blamed by much of the public for an economic downturn and poor law enforcement in the crime-ridden financial sector.

Party leaders nominated Klaus's chief cabinet adviser, economist Jiri Weigl, as Kocarnik's replacement last Saturday but the private Czech television station TV Nova said on Wednesday that Waigl had refused the offer..
Pilip has fought a pitched battle with disgruntled teachers unhappy about the state of the education system.
"In a way, it's replacing one of Klaus's boys with another," said one Czech market analyst.
